questions.question: Distinguish between coupon rate and market interest rate. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Distinguish between coupon rate and market interest rate.
  • - Coupon Rate: The fixed annual interest rate paid by the bond issuer, calculated as a
  • percentage of the bond’s face (par) value. It remains constant throughout the bond’s
  • life. Market Interest Rate: The prevailing rate of return demanded by investors for
  • similar bonds in the open market. It fluctuates based on economic conditions,
  • inflation, and central bank policies.

questions.solution_html:
• What is the role of depositories in the structure of the Indian capital market?
  • Depositories (like NSDL and CDSL) hold securities (shares, bonds) in electronic
  • (dematerialized) form. Their role is to enable seamless, secure, and rapid transfer of
  • ownership, eliminate the risks of physical certificates (theft, forgery, damage), and
  • reduce paperwork and transaction costs.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Random Walk Model and Effecient Market Hypothesis? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the relationship between Random Walk Model and Efficient Ma rket
  • Hypothesis?
  • The Random Walk Model suggests that stock price changes are independent,
  • random, and unpredictable. This is a direct mathematical implication of the Efficient
  • Market Hypothesis (EMH), which states that asset prices fully reflect all avai lable
  • information. Because new information arrives randomly, price adjustments must
  • also be random, making it impossible to consistently "beat the market" through
  • prediction.

• How does the Single Index Model simplify portfolio analysis compared wi th the
  • Markowitz model?
  • The Markowitz model requires calculating the covariance between every possible
  • pair of assets , which is computationally massive for large portfolios. The Single
  • Index Model simplifies this by assuming that all securities are corre lated only
  • through their common relationship with a single market index. This reduces the
  • required estimates to just expected return, beta, and residual variance for each asset,
  • plus the market's expected return and variance , making it highly practical .(liberal
  • valuation)
